title: Parsing date strings safely
when: Dates arrive as text (CSV imports, typed input, old records) in formats like 17/10/2026, 2026-10-17 or 10/17/2026 and must become reliable values.
inputs: whether the source is day first or month first
prompt:
Goal: Explicit, format driven parsing that rejects impossible and ambiguous dates instead of guessing.
Steps:
1. Use new Date(string) only for full ISO 8601 with an offset; write one parser per known format.
2. Anchored regexes per format, such as /^(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})$/ and /^(\d{1,2})\/(\d{1,2})\/(\d{4})$/, with DMY or MDY fixed by the source, never guessed per value.
3. Check month 1 to 12 and day within that month (leap year: divisible by 4 and not 100, or by 400); bound the year.
4. Expand two digit years with a pivot (00 to 49 as 2000s) only when the source uses them.
5. Return { y, m, d } or "YYYY-MM-DD", else null with a reason; attach the source zone before turning date times into instants.
6. For typed input prefer <input type="date">, whose value is already YYYY-MM-DD.
Quality bar:
- 31/02/2026 is rejected, not rolled into March.
- Failures say which part is wrong.
- Tests cover leap days and month ends.
Pitfalls:
- Date rolling invalid days into the next month.
- Guessing DMY or MDY per row.
- Date.parse on non ISO text, which differs between engines.
Verify:
- [ ] Anchored regex per format.
- [ ] Day checked against the month.
- [ ] 29/02 tested in leap and common years.
- [ ] No new Date(userText).
Output: js/parse-date.js exporting parseDate(text, { format }) and tests.

examples.input: o csv do banco tem datas 05/03/2026 e meu app lê como 3 de maio
examples.output: parseDate(text, { format: "DMY" }) with range checks, null plus reason, tests for 29/02
